questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Somewhere culturally exiting with life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was decent upon arrival with mails being sent in advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome day, where we got most of the needed information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Found something through airbnb. It can be pretty hard/expensive to find housing in Paris, so start early!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start early, and don't live on campus, everyone we met who did kind of hated it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Extremely bad, i had to show up at the professors offices when I got there, because i couldn't get the needed info online/through mail.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Really bad, you have to mail the profesors individually, and you cant trust whats available on the website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an office, but they're so busy with all the arrivals, and bad at english.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I got merit for 2/3 of what i hoped for, so I cant complain.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early. Mail professors individually, be a little ruthless.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Either quite hard or way too easy, no in between really. the style of teaching was very high-school-like.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The BA courses were way too easy. Some of the MA's wee pretty hard, but nothing you cant handle when you're used to polit.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Small classrooms, presentations, very much like high school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban and real estate economics Macroeconomics I : Growth and
Overlapping Generation Model Microeconomics I : Choice and Decision
Theory Resource and environmental economics Macroeconomics (Online) Applications of econometrics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Micro and Macro for merit. Urban and real estate economics was pretty interesting. Resource and environmental economics a giant waste of time imo, but good for ects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets more expensive than i assumed, especially in inner Paris. Eating out was relatively cheap though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a gym and some exercise classes you could join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was quite a lot, mostly targeted towards people living on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Gym is the only one I used.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: So much to see in and around Paris, all (public) museums free. Just a great city, you wont be bored.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was very much in a bubble with other exchange students, so not as hard as it could’ve been.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do it through activities; school, sport, chess etc. The locals are nice but pretty reserved, they same way us danes are. Just going up and talking will rarely do it, so do it through common interests.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Bureaucracy, loads of it. random demonstrations. And the way school was taught sucked a bit.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The café lifestyle, a real sense of 'life' in Paris especially. Great food and wine at relatively cheap restaurants on every corner.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to figure most things out yourself, youre going to miss KU's system, and that says a lot. But imo it is still 100% worth it. Don't live on campus, live in paris, even with the extra cost. You didn't come all this way to live in a random town outside of the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living on my own in a foreign city. Having a bit of a 'second home' outside of Copenhagen. Met some great people as well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Bureaucracy

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
